quotes.text: The default Payment Element integration includes a Link prompt in the card form.
Prefilled values are never stored unless the customer completes a Link sign-up.
We only store the prefilled information if the customer takes action and provides consent to create a Link account.
Link supports credit cards, debit cards, and qualified US bank account purchases.
They use the same transaction settlement time and processing behavior as card and bank account payments.

old_evidence.text: the same transaction settlement time and guarantees as card and bank account payments.
Any other 6 digits not listed below

findings: Both captures describe the browser Payment Element: the default card form includes a Link prompt, merchant payment method settings control it, and customers already logged into Link can autofill details originally saved with another business. If the merchant already has the email, pass it via elements.create('payment', {defaultValues: {billingDetails: {email}}}); name and address are optional billing data in the examples. Otherwise, the shopper can enter an email and authenticate or enroll in the Element without integration changes, with an eligible supported payment method for the unsaved-details prompt and customer choice. Old/new raw 9–60 and source 13–28. This is a Link account UI and customer data path, separate from checkout confirmation and payment state.

Both captures distinguish accelerated sign-up, default expanded fields with its own Payment Methods/Link or Connected Accounts settings and customer-country, privacy-law and opt-out qualifications, from the independently disableable Dashboard prefill tool, default when Link is enabled. Same-page detection applies when Stripe customer data has not been supplied programmatically. The guide's prose uses `defaultValue` in that sentence, while the actual Web Elements example uses `defaultValues`. Login receives email for OTP and page information is not stored in that path. Sign-up can prefill email, phone or name, is held temporarily in session memory rather than cookies or local storage and persistence requires customer action and consent to create a Link account. Old/new raw 25–35, 62–91 and source 30–43.

Both captures warn to treat publishable-key-associated sandbox Link accounts as public, use no real user data and authenticate sandbox accounts created with any valid email. Success applies to any other six digits, with 000001 invalid, 000002 expired and 000003 max attempts. Old/new raw 93–106; current source 45–47. Checkout comparison is confined to the matching code outcomes in raw/stripe-checkout-link-2025.md:94–105 and raw/stripe-payments-link-checkout-link-2026-11-07.md:79–91.

Table reflow, quote/comma style, whitespace, an illustration CDN URL and prefill spelling are presentational. The extra custom-checkout before-payment query link at new raw 117 is navigation and supplies no extra workflow authority.

New raw 108–110 describes the same settlement time and processing behavior for additional funding sources as card and bank payments, continuing automatic support without integration changes. The source omits the distinction, and the revised wording supplies no independent proof of guarantee terms, actual settlement, availability, or changes to payment outcomes.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-element-link, the browser Payment Element defaults to a Link prompt in the card form, with merchant control in payment method settings. A customer already logged into Link can autofill details saved through another business. Stripe recommends supplying a known email through defaultValues.billingDetails.email, with name and address available as optional billing details. The in-form email collection route requires no code change. Returning Link customers can use the form to authenticate and populate their saved details. An unenrolled customer who chooses a supported payment method is prompted to save their details and can choose whether to enroll. See old raw lines 15-24 and new raw lines 16-25 for the route conditions, and old raw lines 9-60 and new raw lines 9-60 for the card UI and programmatic billing examples. In old raw lines 62-91 and new raw lines 62-91, accelerated sign-up expands enrollment fields by default with country, legal and customer opt-out conditions. The separately configurable prefill tool defaults on when Link is enabled. Its same-page detection requires Stripe customer data to be absent from supplied defaults, uses session-local memory, stores no page data for returning login and persists new enrollment details only after action and consent. source-stripe-payment-element-link.md lines 13-43 preserve the two routes and local memory but blur the controls and omit eligibility and consent conditions. For sandbox Link authentication, 000001 is invalid, 000002 is expired, 000003 exceeds maximum attempts, and any other six digits succeed. Treat sandbox Link accounts tied to the publishable key as publicly available, use no real user data and use any valid email to create the account, as documented in old raw lines 93-106 and new raw lines 93-106. The current summary at lines 45-47 needs those precise sandbox outcomes. Authentication and enrollment are distinct from payment confirmation and settlement outcomes.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/payment-element-link, old raw lines 93-110 and new raw lines 93-110 establish two material documentation shifts. The listed credit cards, debit cards and qualified US bank purchases lose the exclusivity wording and the registration sentence. The additional-funding comparison replaces guarantees with processing behavior while retaining the same transaction settlement time and automatic support. Preserve both May claims as dated. The separate November registration overview expressly includes Link in Elements and Checkout's embeddable payment form (raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-pmd-registration-2026-11-07.md lines 5-14). Place reciprocal warnings between the route and registration overview so readers have both the dated omission and the separate affirmative scope. The edits establish wording changes. Current live eligibility, specific guarantee terms and actual outcomes still require separate evidence. Table reflow, snippet punctuation and the CDN image change are presentation. The extra before-payment custom checkout link in new raw lines 112-117 beyond old raw lines 112-116 is navigation. Independently, source-stripe-payment-element-link.md lines 30-47 and the Link concept need to distinguish the controls and authentication outcomes already documented in both captures. Customer country, privacy law and customer opt-out qualify accelerated sign-up. The separate page-scanning prefill tool defaults on when Link is enabled, can be disabled in the Dashboard and scans the surrounding checkout page when Stripe customer data has not already been supplied. The scanning prose spells the parameter in the singular as defaultValue, while the Web Elements browser example shows plural defaultValues (old raw lines 24-35 and 71-91, new raw lines 25-35 and 71-91). Keep detected data in the documented session-local and consent boundaries, and keep fixed OTP outcomes scoped to sandbox authentication. This browser route and its test codes do not establish an SDK revision, native or hosted behavior, a server-confirmation contract, payment success or available funds.
